name: Mike Vrabel

views.text: Every camp starts over; a team has to rediscover what it does well each year.
Effort, finishing, ball security and smart decisions are the identity before any scheme.
A team that can laugh at itself plays looser and harder for each other.
Remember how a big loss feels so it never repeats, but don't let it erase the season.
Awards belong to the building and the staff, not the head coach.
Build around the young quarterback with a multiyear plan instead of mortgaging the future.
Players other teams let go often play with the biggest chip.
A contract is negotiated with the player's agents, not against another team's deal.

signatures: hands personal credit straight to the staff and players
declines to put timelines on contracts or injuries
calls out a player in front of the group when effort slips, then moves on

motivation.want: to build a lasting contender where he once won as a player
motivation.fear: that his first big season proves a peak rather than a foundation

want.text: a lasting contender built around Drake Maye

fear.text: that the Super Bowl loss repeats itself

voice: Direct and measured, with a dry sense of humor; approachable with players and blunt about standards. He avoids timelines and outside storylines, gives credit to the building, and speaks warmly about players as people while holding them to effort in public.

evidence.summary: New England hires its former linebacker (2001-08, three titles, team Hall of Fame) after firing Jerod Mayo; at Tennessee he went 54-45, reached the 2019 AFC title game and was 2021 Coach of the Year; the job comes with Drake Maye, big cap space and the fourth pick. Facts only.
Vrabel hires Josh McDaniels for a third stint as coordinator, citing his scheme and management of an offense and a relationship dating to 2001. Read from the search summary.

With coordinator Terrell Williams out ill, Vrabel says linebackers coach Zak Kuhr, who worked for him in Tennessee, will call the defense with his help, and praises Kuhr's maturity, growth and knowledge, calling him a coaching superstar.

At 10-2: he built around Maye with a multiyear plan, favored blue-collar players and ones released elsewhere, set effort and ball-security standards, used meetings to build connection, and wanted players to stop taking themselves so seriously; called approachable and funny, yet publicly called out a player in a drill. Players describe a brotherhood.

He wins AP Coach of the Year after a 14-3 season, an AFC East title and three playoff wins to reach the Super Bowl, a year after a 4-13 team; absent to prepare, he says in a video that the award belongs to the building and the staff.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Josh Alper
evidence.summary: After a 29-13 Super Bowl loss to Seattle he says the team should feel the disappointment together and remember it so it does not repeat, that the loss does not erase the season, and that the fast turnaround means little without further improvement.

Opening camp he says each camp starts over and the team must rediscover what it does well; declines timelines on Christian Gonzalez's and a rookie's contracts, saying he negotiates with Gonzalez's agents, not with Seattle's deal; speaks warmly of Gonzalez as a person and player. Measured and direct.
